Hackers activate automatic defrosting in supermarket fridges across Europe

Hackers activate automatic defrosting in supermarket fridges across Europe

科技产品 作者 Zeekaas 热度 897 回复 997 2026/10/12 20:16
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • (Image credit: AFP)
  • An ongoing cyberattack has reportedly struck major supermarket chains across Europe, disrupting refrigeration control systems. The attack — which has reportedly seen units set to continuously defrost at 50 degrees Celsius — is also apparently affecting deliveries and in-store pricing powered by electronic shelf labels, La Dépêche reports.According to the report, "several" major retailers have been targeted by a cyberattack, which has hit Danfoss-made refrigeration controls used by French supermarkets Intermarché, Leclerc, and Coopérative U. Indeed, the latter's president, Dominique Schelcher, has confirmed as of Monday morning that "A cyberattack has been affecting the refrigeration production facilities of several stores in our network since last night." Schelcher said teams had been mobilized to fix the issue and promised an investigation into the incident, which he described as "extremely serious."Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

flinth_ 2026/10/13 17:38
Well, from my understanding, the write-up by the security company posted in the sub-tweet explain that it's not only the current date, it's just a weak algorithm that only uses the current date as seed, and only that. And this mechanism is complementary to regular auth, so admin password was _something_ but the bypass allowed you (if you reverse engineered the algorithm) to login without knowing it.

So that's still a firmware issue indeed for me, no admin set voluntarly its password to current date.

The write-up in question: https://claroty.com/team82/research/freeze-the-controller-de...

LoganDark 2026/10/13 19:11
IIRC, DMCA does not cover authentication bypass for administration of hardware. It covers circumvention of security measures expressly designed to deter access to copyrighted material, which means it would only apply in the case that the attackers used the exploit to access protected copyrighted material. It's unclear how that would apply to controlling a freezer's setpoint.
